title: Advanced Network Architecture and Dependencies
summary: Interpret a multi-segment topology, dependencies, and failure boundaries in a safe simulation.
objectives: Interpret physical and logical network paths in a multi-segment simulated topology.
Identify service dependencies and possible single points of failure.

vocab.def: A set of components that may be affected by the same failure.
A service or component needed by another service or component.

sections.heading: Prepare
sections.body: This is an authorized network simulation. It does not grant production access or permission to scan, intercept, or change real systems.

sections.heading: Apply
sections.body: Topology text equivalent: Client A connects to Access Switch 1, then to Aggregation Switch 1. A second path connects Client B through Access Switch 2 to Aggregation Switch 2. The aggregation layer connects to two synthetic service networks and a storage network. Solid path labels identify logical links; rack and power notes identify physical dependencies.

sections.heading: Prove
sections.body: Record which path and dependency are supported by the scenario evidence, and label other conclusions as uncertain.

practice.prompt: What should you inspect before claiming a redundant path exists?
practice.answer: Trace both logical paths and verify their shared devices, links, and dependencies.

quiz.question: What is a failure domain?
options: A set of components that may share one failure
A guarantee that a service never stops
A password for a network device
quiz.answer: A set of components that may share one failure

lab.objective: Interpret a synthetic topology and dependency map.

reflectionPrompt: Which observations were supported by the topology, and which required escalation?

careerConnection.text: This is supervised educational infrastructure practice, not professional qualification.
